relatedSnapshot.title: Conferencing setting: “Static meeting link” cannot be disabled and meeting link cannot be cleared
relatedSnapshot.description:
In **Workspace Settings → Conferencing**, the option **“Static meeting link (Same link for all meetings)”** cannot be turned off. Additionally, the meeting link field does not persist deletions: when a user enters a client’s Name 3 Meet link and later deletes it, the link reappears or is not actually removed after saving/reloading.

This prevents users from disabling static links and creates incorrect behavior where a previously entered meeting link remains active even after being cleared.

User: Name 2

Slack: <url:fegrowthpartner.slack.com>

**Impact**

* Users cannot switch away from a static meeting link setup.
* Users may unintentionally keep using an outdated or incorrect meeting link for meetings.
* Confusing and breaks expected “save” behavior for workspace settings.

### Testing

**Repro steps**

 1. Open the app and navigate to a specific workspace (example: Company Three).
 2. Go to **Settings → Conferencing**.
 3. Observe the toggle: **“Static meeting link (Same link for all meetings)”**.
 4. Try to turn the toggle **off**, then **Save**.
 5. Refresh the page or navigate away and back.
 6. Enter a valid meeting link (example: a Name 3 Meet URL) into the static meeting link input.
 7. **Save**.
 8. Delete the meeting link value so the field is empty.
 9. **Save** again.
10. Refresh / revisit the page.

**Expected**

* Toggle state persists: if turned off and saved, it remains off when returning.
* If the meeting link input is cleared and saved, it stays empty when returning.
* When toggle is off, the static meeting link should not be used by the scheduling/booking flow.

**Actual**

* Toggle cannot be turned off (or reverts to on after save/reload).
* Deleted meeting link is not removed (reappears or persists).

**Test variations**

* Repeat in multiple workspaces to confirm setting is truly workspace-scoped.
* Test with multiple users (owner/admin) if roles exist.
* Test on Chrome and Safari.

### Definition of Done

* User can successfully toggle **Static meeting link** on/off in **Settings → Conferencing**, and the state persists after save, refresh, and re-login.
* User can clear the static meeting link input, save, and it remains cleared after refresh/navigation.
* Backend persists `null`/empty value correctly (no fallback re-population unless explicitly intended).
* When static meeting link is **off**, meeting creation/booking does **not** use the static link.
* Add automated coverage:
  * Unit/integration test verifying update + persistence of conferencing settings (toggle and link value).
  * E2E test verifying UI save and reload behavior for toggle + clearing link.
* Confirm workspace isolation: changing conferencing settings in one workspace does not affect another workspace.

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix automation errors in AI-SDR cold email campaign
relatedSnapshot.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 4

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Name 4

#### Screenshot

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Run a standard AI-SDR cold email campaign with automated meeting booking so prospects who reply can easily schedule calls using the connected calendar and Zoom meeting link.  The goal is for the AI to respond to replies and allow prospects to book one valid meeting within the allowed calendar window (9am–5pm CST).

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

The client launched an AI-SDR campaign inside Acquisity.  Steps taken:  • Configured AI campaign using the standard AI configuration template • Connected calendar for automated meeting booking • Set calendar rules to allow booking 9am–5pm CST only • Added Zoom meeting link inside AI configuration • Assigned the correct salesperson calendar (Name 5) • Campaign was turned on and began receiving replies  Campaign produced 14 positive replies within the first week.

#### What is happening instead?

Multiple automation and booking errors are occurring:  • AI sending multiple meeting invites to the same prospect • Prospects receiving duplicate booking links in the same thread • Prospects receiving multiple calendar invites across different days • AI referencing incorrect dates in emails • AI offering calendar times that are actually blocked • Calls being booked outside the allowed time window • Zoom link sometimes sending <domain> instead of the configured meeting link  Additional UI / workflow issues:  • If a prospect CCs another person, the CC contact does not appear in the Acquisity UI • One email thread is locked and cannot be opened or replied to • AI responded to a thread even though it was flagged for manual response  The client paused the campaign because these issues were causing confusion with prospects.

#### What is the expected outcome?

Expected behavior:  • AI should send one booking link only • Prospects should receive one meeting invite • Calendar should only offer available times within the allowed window • Meeting invite should include the correct Zoom link • If a thread is flagged for manual response, AI should not reply automatically • CC recipients should be visible in the Acquisity UI • Email threads should remain clickable and editable  Campaign should run normally without sending duplicate invites or incorrect scheduling information.

relatedSnapshot.title: Manual AI SDR events omit "Join Meeting" button in booking notification email (static/custom conferencing link)
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:
Customer (Name 8, <email>) reports that AI SDR auto-booked meetings send a notification email with both "Join Meeting" and "View Conversation" buttons, but meetings created manually inside an AI SDR conversation ("Create Appointment from Thread") send an email with only "View Conversation" — the "Join Meeting" button is missing, even though Zoom conferencing is configured.

Confirmed root cause in code + prod DB:

* The email template `packages/mail/src/templates/ai-sdr-booking-notification-email.tsx` only renders the "Join Meeting" button when the `meetingUrl` prop is present/safe.
* `bookingService.bookAppointment` derives `meetingUrl` from `videoMeetingManager.resolveMeetingLocation` (`apps/web/lib/scheduling/services/video-meeting-manager.ts`). That function only resolves a `meetingUrl` when the passed `location` is empty or exactly `'zoom_video'`. If a concrete link/string is passed as `location`, it skips the block and `meetingUrl` stays undefined (the link is stored only in `location`).
* Auto-booking (`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/steps/booking.ts`) calls `bookAppointment` with NO `location`, so for a static-link user it sets `meetingUrl = conferencingStaticLink` -> button shows.
* Manual flow (`apps/web/components/ai-sdr/create-appointment-from-thread-modal.tsx` -> `appointments.createFromThread` -> `bookAppointment`): when `conferencingPreferences.linkType === 'static'`, the modal hides the "Zoom Video" option, forces `locationType='custom'`, and pre-fills `customLocation` with the static link. On submit it passes that link as `location`. `resolveMeetingLocation` then skips (location is a real URL, not `'zoom_video'`), so `meetingUrl` is undefined -> email shows only "View Conversation". Both paths send the same email (gate is `if (threadId)` in booking-service.ts).
* Prod DB confirms this user: `conferencing_link_type = 'static'`, `conferencing_static_link = <url:us05web.zoom.us>`. So the static-link branch is exactly what they hit.

Net: a valid Zoom link exists on the appointment (in `location`) but the notification email's "Join Meeting" button is suppressed for manual events because it keys off `meetingUrl`, which the manual/static/custom path never populates.

POTENTIAL FIX:

* In `bookAppointment`/notification, fall back to the resolved `location` (when it is a safe URL) for the email's `meetingUrl` prop when `meetingUrl` is empty; OR
* In `resolveMeetingLocation`, when a static/custom link is supplied as `location`, also set `meetingUrl` to that link (for static-link users, mirror the auto-booking behavior); OR
* Have the email template fall back to a safe `location` URL when `meetingUrl` is absent.
  Ensure this stays consistent with static vs dynamic conferencing and with the calendar event link.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

* Decide which layer owns the fallback (resolveMeetingLocation vs booking-service email props vs email template).
* Confirm expected behavior for custom non-URL locations (physical address) so the button isn't shown for non-join locations.
* Regression tests covering static-link + manual createFromThread producing a Join Meeting button.

INTERCOM: <url:app.intercom.com>
SLACK THREAD: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
DEVIN SESSION: <url>

**Conversation context**: CS teammate (Jam) reports on behalf of the workspace owner that Acquisity-generated Zoom meetings consistently appear four hours later than the matching Acquisity and Name 3 Calendar appointments. Workspace Availability, Name 3 Calendar and the Zoom profile are all America/New_York. Directly created Zoom meetings are correct.

Examples given:

* "G City": Acquisity/Name 3 Calendar 2026-09-16 10:30 AM Eastern -> Zoom shows 2:30 PM
* "Name 11": Acquisity/Name 3 Calendar 2026-09-18 11:00 AM Eastern -> Zoom shows 3:00 PM

**Testable claim**: When Acquisity creates a dynamic Zoom meeting, it sends a UTC (`Z`) start_time together with a local `timezone` field, so Zoom re-applies the workspace's UTC offset: an appointment stored at 2026-09-16T14:30:00Z (10:30 AM Eastern) produces a Zoom meeting shown at 2:30 PM Eastern, four hours late, while directly created Zoom meetings are correct.

**Feature area**: AI SDR / CRM booking -> conferencing (Zoom).

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: Resuming AI SDR does not re-run it, so the response-timeout monitor re-escalates the thread
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When an operator returns an AI SDR thread to automation - Resume AI SDR after an escalation, dismissing an escalation back to automated, or re-enabling the AI SDR toggle - the AI SDR never processes the prospect reply that is still waiting. The response-timeout monitor escalates the thread again within about 15 minutes, it reads as AI SDR Disabled / Needs Attention again, and prospects stay unanswered for days. The operator cannot hand a conversation back to the AI SDR.

## Problem

From the operator's side: they review an escalated thread, resolve the reason it escalated, resume the AI SDR, and it is escalated again within one monitor tick with no AI SDR attempt. The same thread loops however often it is resumed, which is reported by customers as the AI SDR switching itself off.

## Root cause

`resumeFromEscalation` and `dismissEscalation` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/ai-sdr.ts` (about lines 1588 and 1516) and the re-enable toggle (about line 860) end at `updateControlLevel` plus `escalationDismissedAt`. None of them emits `ai-sdr-v2/message.received`, the only trigger of `aiSdrV2Workflow` (`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/workflow.ts`), so the pending prospect reply is never processed.

`monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout.ts` (`check-for-timeouts`, cron `*/15 * * * *`) then escalates any `controlLevel='automated'` thread whose newest recorded message is an inbound reply older than 2 hours and which has never booked, and it never reads `escalation_dismissed_at`. The resume is therefore undone at the next tick.

Scope note for the fix: ENG-8377 ("AI SDR: Allow automation to resume after escalation", Done) defines Resume as making "the next inbound prospect reply" pass the eligibility check, so not re-running the AI SDR for the pending reply was the shipped intent. That points at the monitor side (honour the resume - the newest resume timestamp in `control_level_history` or `escalation_dismissed_at` - or reset the 2-hour clock on resume) unless product decides Resume should also process the pending reply.

## Blast radius

Counted 2026-09-28, 45-day window, all organizations: 2104 resume-then-re-escalation pairs, 1105 distinct threads, 275 distinct organizations, 258 distinct operator users. An independent recount with the same pairing logic returned a slightly higher 2802 pairs / 1208 threads / 280 organizations / 263 users, so the recorded figure is conservative. In every pair measured, zero AI SDR agent executions occur between the resume and the re-escalation.

Query: pairs where a `crm_message_thread.control_level_history` entry `to='automated'` from `'escalated'` or `'human_takeover'` is followed within 2 hours by an entry `to='escalated'` with `updatedBy='monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout'` (jsonb_array_elements joined on thread_id, `m.ts > r.ts AND m.ts <= r.ts + interval '2 hours'`), left-checked against `agent_executions` in the interval.

Potentially exposed: every thread an operator returns to automated after an escalation.

## Proposed fix

Make the either/or explicit and implement it: a thread returned to automated must not be re-escalated by the response-timeout monitor before the AI SDR has had a chance on it. Either honour the resume when evaluating timeout candidates, or trigger the AI SDR on resume for the pending reply.

## What's included

The monitor/resume decision and its regression test. Related, not included: ENG-14111 (a sent AI SDR reply is never recorded, which the same monitor also turns into an escalation) and ENG-10060 (periodic provider-versus-local thread/message reconciliation).

## Regression seam

`check-for-timeouts` in `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout.ts`. Red before: a thread whose control level returned to `automated` with no new inbound is escalated by the monitor at the next tick. Green after: such a thread is not escalated, or, if Resume is redefined, the AI SDR runs for the pending reply. `apps/web/tests/lib/inngest/functions/monitor-ai-sdr-response-timeout-db.test.ts` already exercises the candidate filters against Postgres and is the place to add the resumed-thread case.

## Done when

* A thread returned to automated after an escalation is not re-escalated by the response-timeout monitor before the AI SDR has acted or the resume has been honoured.
* No prospect reply is left unanswered because a resume silently did nothing.
* A regression test proves the behaviour at the named seam.

## Reports

* ENG-14415

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR pauses booking for assigned host Name 12: Zoom shows connected but is invalid, no static fallback
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom source: **<url:app.intercom.com>

**Customer:** Name 1 — "Name 1's Workspace"

## Claim

The workspace's AI SDR assigned call handler (Name 12, set to Zoom-connect mode) has a Zoom account that is marked disconnected in the backend while the settings UI still shows Zoom as connected, and has no static meeting-link fallback, so the AI SDR pauses booking with "meeting location unavailable" instead of booking confirmed meetings.

## Context

The customer says their sales agent Name 100 already has his Zoom link set in the app, but the AI SDR is not booking meetings. Separately, when they create an appointment manually from a thread and pick Name 100 as host, Name 100's meeting link and email are not auto-filled (the location pre-fills with the owner's own static link instead).

## What we found

* Name 100 is this workspace's assigned AI SDR call handler, in Zoom-connect (dynamic) mode with no static link.
* Name 100's Zoom account is marked invalid (disconnected) in the backend as of 2026-08-27, even though the conferencing UI presents it as connected.
* The owner's account has a static Riverside link set, but it belongs to the owner, not Name 100.
* The AI SDR therefore cannot resolve a meeting location for Name 100 and escalates rather than booking (the fail-closed behavior shipped to prevent linkless bookings).

See the attached Triage investigation document for the full production-data, code-path, and blast-radius readout.
